questionText: State one function for each of the parts labelled I, II, IX and X in Fig. 1(a).
modelAnswer:
I (Aorta): Carries oxygenated blood from the heart/left ventricle to the rest of the body[cite: 121, 130].
II (Pulmonary vein): Brings oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium[cite: 121, 130].
IX (Vena cava): Brings deoxygenated blood from the body to the right atrium[cite: 121, 130].
X (Pulmonary artery): Carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs[cite: 121, 130].

questionText: Explain briefly why the left lower part of the heart has a thicker muscle.
modelAnswer: It contracts to pump oxygenated blood under high pressure to all parts of the body[cite: 121, 130].

questionText: State two ways by which the flow of blood to and from the mammalian heart as shown in Fig. 1(a) can be kept at acceptable levels.
modelAnswer:
1. Regular physical exercise[cite: 121, 130].
2. Eating a balanced diet and avoiding smoking[cite: 121, 130].

questionText: Name two parts of the heart where oxygenated blood can be found.
modelAnswer: Left atrium and left ventricle[cite: 121, 130].

questionText: Describe briefly how each of the parts labelled P, Q and R are planted on seedbed.
modelAnswer:
P (Maize): Make holes using a stick/dibber, place 2-3 seeds per hole, and cover with soil[cite: 122, 130].
Q (Tomato seedlings): Remove a seedling gently from the nursery, place it in a prepared hole, firm the soil around it, and water immediately[cite: 122, 130].
R (Cassava cuttings): Dig trenches/holes and place the stem cuttings into the soil at an angle with nodes facing upward, then firm the soil[cite: 122, 130].

questionText: State four conditions under which R can be cultivated to produce high yield.
modelAnswer:
1. Adequate rainfall/irrigation[cite: 122, 130].
2. Fertile soil with good structure[cite: 122, 130].
3. Adequate sunlight[cite: 122, 130].
4. Absence of pests and diseases[cite: 122, 130].

questionText: State one function for each of the parts labelled I, II, III and IV in Fig. 1(c).
modelAnswer:
I (Cell/Battery): Converts chemical energy to electrical energy (generates voltage)[cite: 122, 131].
II (Switch/Key): Opens and closes the circuit to allow or stop current flow[cite: 122, 131].
III (Connecting wire): Allows charges/current to flow between components[cite: 122, 131].
IV (Resistor): Opposes the flow of electrical charges/current[cite: 122, 131].

questionText: If the voltmeter reads 2.4 V and the ammeter reads 0.8 A when the circuit is closed, calculate the value of the part labelled IV.
modelAnswer: Resistance (R) = V / I = 2.4 / 0.8 = 3 Ω[cite: 123, 131].

questionText: State one way of conserving the value of the part labelled I in the circuit.
modelAnswer: Open the key/switch when not taking readings[cite: 123, 131].

questionText: State two observations that can be made when the circuit is closed.
modelAnswer:
1. Ammeter deflects/reads current[cite: 123, 131].
2. Voltmeter deflects/reads voltage[cite: 123, 131].

questionText: Describe briefly the process of this experiment shown in Fig. 1(d).
modelAnswer: Pour the immiscible liquid mixture into the separating funnel, allow it to stand until it separates into two distinct layers, open the tap to drain the lower liquid layer into a conical flask, and close the tap once separated[cite: 123, 131].

questionText: State one function for each of the parts labelled II and IV in Fig. 1(d).
modelAnswer:
II (Stopcock/Tap): Regulates or controls the flow of liquid[cite: 123, 131].
IV (Retort stand): Holds and supports the separating funnel firmly[cite: 123, 131].

questionText: State two precautions that should be taken to obtain reliable results when performing this experiment.
modelAnswer:
1. Open the tap gently to release only the bottom liquid layer[cite: 123, 131].
2. Allow the mixture sufficient time to settle and separate completely into layers[cite: 123, 131].

questionText: Given a flashlight, a tennis ball and a screen; draw a diagram to show how a shadow can be formed.
modelAnswer: A setup showing a flashlight casting light on a tennis ball, creating an umbra and penumbra shadow on a screen[cite: 124, 132].

questionText: A student seeking to determine the volume of an irregular body of mass 4 kg used a graduated cylinder in an experiment (Fig. 2). Determine the density of the irregular body.
modelAnswer:
Volume change = 75 cm³ - 50 cm³ = 25 cm³ (0.000025 m³).
Density = Mass / Volume = 4 kg / 25 cm³ = 160 kg cm⁻³ (or 160 g cm⁻³)[cite: 124, 132].

questionText: State two precautions that must be taken to obtain reliable results.
modelAnswer:
1. Drop the irregular body gently into the cylinder to avoid splashing water[cite: 124, 132].
2. Read the volume at the correct meniscus level[cite: 124, 132].

questionText: State three safety precautions to prevent accidents during the use of liquefied petroleum gas in the home.
modelAnswer:
1. Store LPG cylinders in a well-ventilated open-air space[cite: 124, 132].
2. Check gas hoses regularly and replace them when worn out[cite: 124, 132].
3. Strike the match before turning on the gas valve[cite: 124, 132].

questionText: Explain briefly the scientific principle underlying composting.
modelAnswer: Microorganisms use oxygen to decompose and break down organic matter into nutrient-rich humus[cite: 125, 132].

questionText: Explain briefly the scientific principle underlying recycling.
modelAnswer: Physical and chemical processing of waste materials to convert them into new usable products[cite: 125, 132].

questionText: Explain briefly the scientific principle underlying incineration.
modelAnswer: Burning waste materials at high temperatures to destroy contaminants and convert them into gas and ash[cite: 125, 132].

questionText: Outline three features that would help to differentiate between the digestive systems of a goat and a rabbit.
modelAnswer:
1. Goats are ruminants with a four-chambered stomach (polygastric), whereas rabbits have a simple one-chambered stomach (monogastric)[cite: 125, 132].
2. Rabbits have a large caecum for cellulose digestion (hindgut fermentation), unlike goats[cite: 125, 132].
3. Differences in dental structure (goats lack upper incisors, rabbits have peg teeth)[cite: 125, 132].

questionText: Design a 4-year rotational program using maize, cowpea, cassava and cabbage.
modelAnswer:
Year 1: Plot 1: Maize, Plot 2: Cowpea, Plot 3: Cassava, Plot 4: Cabbage
Year 2: Plot 1: Cabbage, Plot 2: Maize, Plot 3: Cowpea, Plot 4: Cassava
Year 3: Plot 1: Cassava, Plot 2: Cabbage, Plot 3: Maize, Plot 4: Cowpea
Year 4: Plot 1: Cowpea, Plot 2: Cassava, Plot 3: Cabbage, Plot 4: Maize[cite: 125, 133].

questionText: Give two reasons for the sequence given in 3(a)(i).
modelAnswer:
1. Breaks pest and disease cycles[cite: 125, 133].
2. Cowpea is a leguminous crop that fixes nitrogen into the soil[cite: 125, 133].

questionText: Calculate the acceleration of the vehicle (mass = 1000 kg, initial velocity = 100 m s⁻¹, final velocity = 150 m s⁻¹, time = 10 s).
Calculate the force that acts on the vehicle.
Calculate the final momentum when the vehicle comes to a stop.
modelAnswer: Final momentum = mass × final velocity = 1000 kg × 0 m s⁻¹ = 0 Ns[cite: 126, 133].

questionText: A student who went to bed immediately after eating complained of stomach upset the next morning. A doctor prescribed a liver salt whose major composition is NaHCO3 as the medication. Using a balanced chemical equation, explain how the liver salt would relieve the student from this discomfort.
modelAnswer: Stomach acid is HCl. Equation: HCl + NaHCO3 → NaCl + H2O + CO2. The liver salt acts as a base that neutralizes excess stomach acid, relieving the pain[cite: 127, 134].

questionText: Calculate the energy of the body placed on top of a wall (mass = 20 kg, height = 10 m, g = 10 m s⁻²).
modelAnswer: Potential Energy (E) = mgh = 20 kg × 10 m s⁻² × 10 m = 2000 J (or 2 kJ)[cite: 127, 134].

questionText: Define the term light emitting diode (LED).
modelAnswer: An LED is a semiconductor device that emits light when an electric current passes through it[cite: 127, 134].

questionText: Mention two devices that use LED in their operation.
modelAnswer:
1. Traffic lights[cite: 127, 134].
2. Smartphone screens / Digital watches[cite: 127, 134].

questionText: Suggest two simple tools that could be used in nursery bed preparation.

1. Hoe[cite: 127, 134].
2. Rake / Shovel / Garden fork[cite: 127, 134].

Rake: Used for leveling the soil surface and removing debris[cite: 127, 134].

questionText: State three observable features of an animal cell.
modelAnswer:
1. Cell membrane[cite: 127, 134].
2. Cytoplasm[cite: 127, 134].
3. Nucleus / Nuclear membrane[cite: 127, 134].

questionText: State two functions of a nerve cell.
modelAnswer:
1. Transmits electrical impulses/messages throughout the body[cite: 127, 134].
2. Responds to physical and chemical stimuli[cite: 127, 134].

questionText: Calculate the effective resistance in the circuit shown in Fig. 5 (parallel resistors of 4 Ω and 5 Ω).
Calculate the current that will flow through the circuit when it is closed (Voltage = 6 V).
Differentiate between an organic fertilizer and an inorganic fertilizer.
modelAnswer: Organic fertilizers are derived from natural plant and animal sources, whereas inorganic fertilizers are manufactured artificially through chemical and physical processes[cite: 129, 134].

questionText: Outline briefly the steps involved in preparing raised beds.
modelAnswer:
1. Clear vegetation and weeds[cite: 130, 134].
2. Dig and loosen the topsoil, breaking large lumps and removing roots/stones[cite: 130, 134].
3. Shape the bed into size, firm the edges, and level the surface with a rake[cite: 130, 134].

questionText: State one function each of the following components of blood: red blood cells, white blood cells, blood plasma.
modelAnswer:
Red blood cells: Carry oxygen from the lungs to body tissues[cite: 130, 134].
White blood cells: Protect the body against infections and diseases[cite: 130, 134].
Blood plasma: Transports nutrients, hormones, wastes, and water throughout the body[cite: 130, 134].

questionText: Explain briefly the impact of each of the following organisms on humans: housefly, grasshopper.
modelAnswer:
Housefly: Helps in the decomposition of organic matter, but also acts as a vector spreading diseases like cholera and dysentery[cite: 130, 134].
Grasshopper: Serves as part of the ecosystem food web, but can cause severe destruction to crops and vegetation[cite: 130, 134].

questionText: Describe briefly the formation of an ammonia molecule after an interaction between H and N atoms.
modelAnswer: Nitrogen (N) has 5 valence electrons and Hydrogen (H) has 1 valence electron. Three H atoms combine with one N atom, with each H atom sharing a covalent bond with one electron from N to form the NH3 molecule[cite: 130].
